docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
SPHinXsim is a Python and LLM-facing workflow for building, visualizing, validating, updating, and running SPH simulations on top of the SPHinXsys C++ library.

The project is designed around explicit simulation configuration rather than opaque prompt-only execution. A user can describe a scenario in natural language, generate a structured JSON config, revise that config with further instructions, validate it against strict schemas, and execute it through the SPHinXsys backend.

docs.title: What this repository provides
docs.text:
• A Python package, sphinxsim, with a CLI for config generation, update, visualization, validation, and execution.
  • Pydantic-based schemas for geometry, materials, particle generation, solver settings, observers, constraints, and recording options.
  • LLM adapters with a local mock backend by default and API service based generation when configured.
  • Native C++ bindings and simulation builders that bridge validated JSON configs to SPHinXsys runtime components.
  • Tests and documentation covering schema rules, CLI behavior, and integrated simulation workflows.

docs.title: Core workflow
docs.text:
For a single desktop window with a JSON editor, PyVista Preview, and embedded Chainlit chat, run python -m sphinxsim workbench. See Desktop Workbench for configuration edits and Agent demonstrations.

SPHinXsim also includes two distinct AI-assisted workflows:

  • Workbench Chat uses the configured LLM and discovered native MCP tools to discuss and propose changes to the open configuration. Review proposals in the JSON Editor before applying or saving them.
  • AgentCAE runs a durable, bounded calibration workflow. It plans candidate cases, asks for approval before execution by default, analyzes saved results, and records a report. The currently supported example calibrates column-collapse runout. Start with python -m sphinxsim agent --help; see AgentCAE calibration for setup and lifecycle instructions.

Both use the provider configured through SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER. The mock provider is useful for deterministic local testing; it is not a natural-language model. See LLM testing for provider setup.

The recommended user workflow is to use the interactive shell:

sphinxsim shell

Inside the shell, you can:

  1. Load an existing config file: load config.json
  2. Generate a simulation config from natural language: generate "water dam break" config.json
  3. Validate the config structure: validate
  4. Update it with further instructions: update "simulate for 2 s"
  5. Explore the simulator schema and capabilities: explore what body types are supported?
  6. Run the validated simulation: run
  7. Update geometry or other fields: update "water flow with 5 mm resolution"
  8. Rerun preview or run to rebuild from the updated config

In shell mode, you can also use slash-prefixed commands without quotes around the description, for example /generate water dam break config.json or /update simulate for 2 s. In shell mode, validate reloads the loaded file from disk so external edits are picked up immediately. Geometry edits stay config-driven in shell mode: update the JSON, then rerun preview or run to rebuild from the current file.

Alternatively, you can use direct commands for non-interactive workflows:

  • sphinxsim generate — Create a config from description
  • sphinxsim update — Modify an existing config
  • sphinxsim explore — Ask schema and functionality questions
  • sphinxsim validate — Check config validity
  • sphinxsim run — Execute a validated simulation
  • sphinxsim preview — Render an interactive geometry/BC preview before running
  • sphinxsim workbench — Open the desktop JSON Editor, Preview, and Chat
  • sphinxsim agent — Manage durable AgentCAE workflows
  • sphinxsim --generate-completion {bash|zsh|fish} — Print shell completion scripts

For detailed examples and all command options, see CLI Usage.

docs.title: High-level architecture
docs.text:
• sphinxsim/cli.py: Command-line entry point for configuration, visualization, native execution, desktop Workbench, MCP, and AgentCAE workflows. It resolves project-local paths, validates configs before execution, and routes runtime output into project-managed build directories.
  • sphinxsim/agent/: Durable AgentCAE planning, approval, execution, analysis, persistence, and bounded calibration workflows. See AgentCAE calibration.
  • sphinxsim/ui/workbench/ and sphinxsim/ui/chatbot/: Desktop JSON editing, preview, and Chat integrations. See AI Workbench.
  • sphinxsim/config/schemas.py: Defines the top-level SimulationConfig and the typed config surface for system domains, global resolution, shapes, oriented boxes, particle generation, fluid bodies, continuum bodies, solid bodies, boundary conditions, observers, restart settings, body constraints, and extra state recording.
  • sphinxsim/llm/: Provides LLM backends that translate natural-language prompts into schema-compliant configs and answer schema exploration questions. The default mock backend supports deterministic local testing, while OpenAI-compatible, NVIDIA, and Ollama backends use the shared SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER, SPHINXSIM_LLM_MODEL, SPHINXSIM_LLM_BASE_URL, and SPHINXSIM_LLM_API_KEY settings.
  • sphinxsim/sph_simulation/ and native bindings: Build and load SPHinXsys-backed simulation objects from validated JSON, including fluid and continuum-oriented workflows exposed through the Python package.

docs.title: Current capabilities
docs.text:
SPHinXsim currently supports a broader config surface than a basic fluid-only demo workflow:

  • Fluid dynamics configurations with typed fluid materials, inflow boundary conditions, observers, and solver controls.
  • Continuum dynamics configurations with continuum material models (including plastic_continuum for soil/granular cases) and dedicated continuum solver parameters.
  • Solid boundary/body definitions required by the current validation and simulation builders.
  • Config-driven geometry composition using domains, shapes, oriented boxes, transforms, and particle-generation settings.
  • Incremental config editing through the CLI update command instead of regenerating cases from scratch.
  • Schema exploration through the CLI explore command for questions about supported bodies, materials, and simulator behavior.
  • LLM-assisted configuration proposals and native MCP tool discovery in the Workbench.
  • Durable AgentCAE calibration with approval checkpoints, persisted runs, result analysis, and reports.

The repository remains config-first: natural-language generation is useful for initialization and revision, but the validated JSON artifact is the authoritative simulation input.

docs.title: Current direction
docs.text: The codebase is positioned for richer multi-physics growth while staying strict about validation boundaries. In practice, that means expanding benchmark coverage, continuing to improve continuum and coupled workflows, and strengthening the path from prompt to executable, testable simulation assets.

docs.title: LLM test matrix
docs.text:
The repository now supports two LLM testing modes:

  • Mocked tests are always safe for CI and run without any external service.
  • Ollama integration tests run locally when Ollama is available and are skipped in CI.

See LLM testing for the exact test matrix, environment variables, and local commands.

docs.title: Why this project matters
docs.text:
SPHinXsys provides strong performance and physical modeling, but direct setup can be expensive for rapid iteration. SPHinXsim narrows that gap by combining:

  • A structured Python interface for orchestration and validation.
  • LLM-assisted config authoring and revision.
  • Native execution against SPHinXsys kernels once the config is validated.

Together, these pieces provide a practical path from idea to executable simulation with clearer structure, stronger reproducibility, and lower onboarding friction.

docs.title: AgentCAE
docs.text:
AgentCAE is a durable orchestration layer using the native SPHinXsim MCP stdio service. It discovers the running tool inventory, plans a bounded workflow, records every candidate case and result, pauses before solver execution when approval is enabled, analyzes VTP artifacts, and adjusts the next candidate until the requested tolerance is met.

The current validated workflow calibrates the friction angle of a two-dimensional granular column collapse to a runout_extension target of 0.2 m. runout_extension means final front minus initial front; it does not mean the absolute final x-coordinate.

docs.title: Control and execution boundaries
docs.text:
AgentCAE separates uncertain reasoning from deterministic execution:

  1. A structured planner proposes a workflow or analysis definition as JSON.
  2. Pydantic schemas and capability registries reject unknown tools, fields, units, bodies, coordinate components, and reductions.
  3. LangGraph controls approval, execution, analysis, search, replanning, and terminal states.
  4. SQLite checkpoints and workflow artifacts allow another Python process to inspect or resume the same workflow without repeating a completed C++ run.
  5. SPHinXsim performs configuration generation, validation, and C++ simulation.
  6. Deterministic streaming readers extract approved metrics from final VTP files.
  7. Before the first solver run, an off-screen particle Preview is reviewed by a multimodal model. This visual preflight can accept the case or request at most one validated regeneration pass; it never measures numerical results.

The LLM never executes the solver and does not directly edit files. Replanning is limited to allow-listed actions such as retrying a transient failure, revising bounded parameter limits, or stopping. Declarative extractors permit only final ASCII VTP Position min/max reductions. Python code, expressions, imports, shell commands, and arbitrary file paths are forbidden by schema.

docs.title: Durable calibration lifecycle
docs.text:
Select the LLM exactly as for the existing generate command. AgentCAE uses the same setting for planning, configuration generation, visual preflight, failure replanning, and extractor planning. For Ollama, select a model that can consume images because visual preflight sends a PNG screenshot:

$env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "mock"       # deterministic local evaluation
# $env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "ollama"   # local Ollama + vision model
# $env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "openai"   # OpenAI API
# $env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "nvidia_nim" # NVIDIA NIM API

Start a workflow. With mock, this tests the production control path without sending data to an external LLM:

python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent start `
  "Calibrate a 2D column-collapse runout extension to 0.2 m." `
  --workflow-id column_020 --json

Inspect, approve, resume, cancel, or report from a later process:

python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent status column_020 --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent approve column_020 --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent resume column_020 --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent cancel column_020 --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent report column_020 --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent execution column_020
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent events column_020
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent results column_020

Approval covers the complete bounded Plan. A durable worker then performs the visual preflight and all required generate/run/analyze/adjust iterations. A report is generated from persisted workflow truth and contains the target, tolerance, visual review evidence, analysis contract, all parameter/metric observations, best result, immutable attempt logs, replanning history, timing, and error state.

docs.title: Parallel Chatbot and Preview windows
docs.text:
When agent approve or agent resume is sent in Chatbot, the solver runs in its durable worker and a separate desktop Preview window observes its output. The window reuses Preview's geometry, model information, gravity, observers, colours, and particle rendering. It never generates particles or starts a second solver. The same particle updater is used by the shell's continue-to-run display.

The window follows new candidate runs automatically and preserves the camera. Its Agent results menu can switch between the current run, the best completed candidate, and individual completed candidates. The final frame remains visible after convergence or cancellation. Closing the window does not cancel the worker. Send agent preview to reopen it. After reopening Chatbot, send agent attach <workflow-id> followed by agent preview to observe an existing run.

Preview opens on the computer running Chatbot; a remote browser does not receive the desktop window. It requires pyvistaqt and PySide6 in that Python environment. Window process diagnostics are written to execution/<workflow-id>/preview.log. The chat retains progress, iteration results, and reports instead of appending a live PNG every five seconds. Opening this window does not change when an LLM receives images: visual preflight still occurs before the first solve, and live frames remain for user observation.

Run the observer regression and actual Qt window smoke test with:

python -m pytest tests/test_agent_preview.py -q

For deterministic evaluation, prepare a JSON response that matches the DeclarativeExtractorSpec schema and use the mock structured-planner boundary:

python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent extractor plan `
  "Measure the final deposit height." `
  --config case.json `
  --response-file extractor-response.json --json

python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent extractor list --json

python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace .build-temp/agent extractor analyze `
  deposit_height case.json path/to/run-directory --json

The planning command validates case.json and derives the body and spatial dimension allow-lists instead of trusting user-supplied declarations. An extractor definition is persisted with a SHA-256 fingerprint. It can be recompiled in another process and applied to a different artifact set with the same body and dimensional contract. The VTP reader streams numeric content and stores bounds and counts; it does not build a full in-memory particle array.

When SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER selects a cloud provider, extractor planning sends the extractor request, listed body names, spatial dimension, allowed operations, and output schema to that configured endpoint. Only use a cloud provider when that bounded data export is authorized.

docs.title: Persisted data
docs.text:
The workspace contains:

workspace/
  checkpoints.sqlite
  runtime/<workflow-id>.json
  execution/events.sqlite
  execution/<workflow-id>/worker.json
  execution/<workflow-id>/attempts/<attempt-id>/
  store/workflows/<workflow-id>/workflow.json
  store/workflows/<workflow-id>/cases/
  store/tasks/<task-id>/
  extractors.json
  reports/<workflow-id>.json

Do not delete or manually change these files while a workflow is active. Use a separate workspace for independent AgentCAE deployments. The RunManager enforces one active solver worker per workspace, verifies process identity before stopping a process tree, and marks orphaned workers as interrupted for explicit resume.

docs.title: Upstream configuration compatibility
docs.text:
Agent validation, extractor planning, Workbench loading, proposals, and saves use the shared native admission checks in sphinxsim.runtime.physics. Native CLI and MCP operations use the same checks. Invalid or inactive material fields therefore produce an error at the editing or planning entry point.

LLM configuration cleanup preserves named box and bounding_box primitive references. Initial-front analysis resolves a named bounding_box primitive and supports inline bounds. It checks reference uniqueness, primitive type, finite ordered bounds, and direction dimensionality. Preview also infers dimensionality from primitives when the domain and gravity are omitted.

Use the upstream configuration locations for new or revised cases.

  • Set surface handling with fluid_bodies[].surface_type.
  • Define a container with polygons[].inner_box, using inline bounds or a named bounding_box primitive.
  • Set solid refinement with particle_generation.bodies[].solid_body.refinement_to_global. The shared admission check reports adaptation_ratios as an inactive field and includes the current configuration path in its error.
  • Reference a relaxation geometry with particle_generation.bodies[].relaxation.level_set.shape.

AgentCAE's RunManager owns workflow orchestration. Native MCP project_inspect, submit, job_status, job_logs, job_cancel, and results_inspect own solver execution on Windows and POSIX. Each workflow run stores the complete job reference in job-reference.json. Reopening a submitted run queries that job. Analysis verifies published hashes and uses the frozen configuration and saved particle sources. Preview rendering uses results_render on a published particle job. Each MCP attempt records its transport, reference, timing, and failure state.

Configuration generation, reviewed editor proposals, case/resource preparation, friction edits, and result extraction use operations registered in sphinxsim.operations.TOOLS. The official MCP SDK client calls the same service available to external clients. The planner receives its discovered tool schemas alongside the calibration contracts and upstream documentation.

The Chatbot discovers native tools for structured LLM tool selection. Real providers can inspect capabilities, author configurations, generate CAD, submit jobs, and inspect results from the conversation. An explicit command such as /mcp capabilities {} also works with the mock provider. Embedded editor changes use workbench and config_propose, followed by the existing proposal review.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text: Run these commands from the repository root in the existing project Python environment. Each stage checks a different part of the Agent workflow.

docs.title: Static review
docs.text:
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git diff

docs.title: Configuration and analysis regression tests
docs.text:
These tests exercise Python configuration admission, primitive preservation, initial-front extraction, planner context, and Workbench document validation.

$env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "mock"
python -m pytest -q tests/runtime/test_configuration.py tests/test_llm.py tests/test_runout_analyzer.py tests/test_extractor_planner.py tests/test_local_knowledge.py tests/test_planner_context.py tests/test_workbench.py -m "not integration"
python -m pytest -q tests/test_visualization.py -k "TestSpatialDimensionInference"
python -m sphinxsim capabilities --json
python -m sphinxsim validate tests/test_simulation/test_2d_simulation/data/column_collapse.json

All selected tests should pass. The configuration tests check equivalent admission through CLI, MCP operations, and compilation, preserve the source file, and exercise refinement and named Level Set dictionaries. Runout tests compare inline and primitive-based initial fronts in 2D and 3D with both direction signs.

docs.title: Deterministic Agent workflow tests
docs.text:
The deterministic adapter supplies particle artifacts for the complete plan/approve/execute/analyze/report cycle. Lifecycle tests also exercise the real CLI and persisted state with the mock LLM provider.

python -m pytest -q tests/runtime/test_agent_tools.py tests/test_mcp_tool_conversation.py tests/test_mock_vertical_workflow.py tests/test_deterministic_calibration_workflow.py tests/test_agent_cae_product_acceptance.py tests/test_agent_cli.py

The vertical acceptance test checks four completed candidates, persisted reports, and convergence. Product acceptance also checks reopening workflows in another facade and controlled failures for unavailable artifacts.

docs.title: Real solver acceptance
docs.text:
Use an environment with the project's existing 2D native extension. This test executes several C++ simulations with a mock LLM provider.

$env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "mock"
$env:SPHINXSIM_RUN_REAL_CALIBRATION = "1"
python -m pytest tests/test_real_calibration_workflow.py -q -k mock_llm
Remove-Item Env:SPHINXSIM_RUN_REAL_CALIBRATION

The acceptance criterion is convergence to 0.2 m with an absolute runout extension error at most 0.005 m within eight unique candidates.

docs.title: Manual lifecycle and desktop checks
docs.text:
Use the existing native extension and visualization dependencies for visual preflight and solver execution. The mock setting supplies LLM responses while the approved workflow runs the native simulator.

$env:SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER = "mock"
$agentWorkspace = ".build-temp/agent-upstream-validation"
$agentWorkflowId = "upstream_" + (Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss")
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace start "Calibrate a 2D column-collapse runout extension to 0.2 m." --workflow-id $agentWorkflowId --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace status $agentWorkflowId --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace approve $agentWorkflowId --background --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace execution $agentWorkflowId
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace events $agentWorkflowId
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace status $agentWorkflowId --json
python -m sphinxsim agent --workspace $agentWorkspace report $agentWorkflowId --json

Before approval, expect awaiting_approval to be true and case_prepared to be false. After the worker finishes, expect status converged, best_absolute_error <= 0.005 in status, and best_result.absolute_error <= 0.005 in the report. Inspect each attempt's stdout.log, stderr.log, and attempt.json under execution/<workflow-id>/attempts/ if a command fails. Open another terminal with the same workspace and workflow ID to check persisted status. cancel requests termination, and resume continues an interrupted running workflow.

Open python -m sphinxsim workbench to check the JSON editor, reviewed LLM proposals, explicit save, Preview, and Agent chat. Preview should select the 2D binding for a case whose dimensions are defined only through named primitives. The optional desktop test exercises the real Qt/chat/preview/solver flow.

$env:SPHINXSIM_RUN_WORKBENCH_DESKTOP = "1"
python -m pytest tests/test_workbench.py -q -k real_workbench_desktop
Remove-Item Env:SPHINXSIM_RUN_WORKBENCH_DESKTOP

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text: The lifecycle and safety architecture is reusable, but the shipped optimization workflow is deliberately narrow: one friction-angle parameter and one runout objective. New simulation families require registered deterministic parameter tools and metric extractors before an LLM may select them. This preserves a clear rule: the model chooses among declared capabilities; Python and C++ own validation, execution, numerical extraction, persistence, and safety limits.

docs.title: Native CLI and external agents
docs.text:
SPHinXsim uses its existing sphinxsim package and CLI for both people and agents. MCP exposes the same application operations. There is no separate agent package, command-line program, required cloud service or container image.

For the built-in durable calibration agent, see AgentCAE calibration. For the desktop editor, Preview, and embedded Chat workflow, see AI Workbench.

For client configuration and resource access, see MCP setup. The optional companion skill follows the repository's .github/skills/ convention. Install the complete sphinxsim skill directory, including its references/, through your agent client's supported mechanism. It guides experiment design and quality interpretation; it grants no access.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Follow the platform installation guide to build the native bindings. From this checkout, install the optional features you need:

python -m pip install '.[dev,cad,mcp,results,visualization]'
sphinxsim --help
python -m sphinxsim --help

cad installs CadQuery/OCCT and mesh validation dependencies. results supplies VTK and mesh boolean support for headless export and quality checks. mcp installs the official MCP Python SDK. visualization supplies the native Qt window. These extras do not replace the compiled SPHinXsim bindings. Basic CLI/schema use does not import CAD, MCP or Qt until requested.

Detached local jobs use native process supervision on Windows and POSIX. Windows workers use hidden console processes and process-identity checks for cancellation. A remote desktop, GPU runtime, display/input provider, authentication gateway and container packaging are the deployment owner's responsibility and are not shipped in this change.

docs.title: Configuration and action authority
docs.text:
Native simulation JSON defines what to simulate. Explicit CLI/MCP operations define what to do. Validation and execution do not rewrite source JSON. Compilation returns a new native configuration, unit conversions and normalization diagnostics; review those before explicitly applying it.

File references resolve within the workspace chosen by the owner. A frozen project includes the entry JSON and the complete admitted resource inventory, including sizes and SHA-256 hashes. A hash alone is not a substitute for the referenced bytes. Raw file hashes and normalized configuration identities have different scopes and must not be substituted for one another.

Use native snake_case JSON keys and the existing positional-file and -o/--output CLI conventions. Structured operations accept bounded JSON input and return { "ok": true, "data": ... } or a JSON error. --json selects machine output; native execution diagnostics go to stderr or bounded job logs.

docs.title: Configuration and CAD
docs.text:
sphinxsim capabilities --json
sphinxsim validate project/config.json --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim compile specification.json -o reviewed-config.json --json
sphinxsim geometry recipe.json -o project/models/candidate --json

Compilation accepts { "version": 1, "configuration": <native configuration> }. Within that structure an explicitly supported quantity may use, for example, "particle_spacing": { "value": 25, "unit": "mm" }. Compilation produces ordinary native numeric JSON; it does not introduce a second physics language. Combining explicit quantities with native characteristic scaling is rejected.

A minimal CAD recipe is:

{
  "version": 1,
  "unit": "mm",
  "operations": [
    {"id": "body", "op": "box", "args": {"size": [2000, 1000, 800]}}
  ],
  "output": "body"
}

Query capabilities.modeling for the bounded operations and parameters, including sketches, extrusion, revolution, loft, sweep, booleans and transforms. CAD accepts data, never arbitrary Python or shell code. It outputs meter-based model.stl, model.step, recipe.json and cad-result.json, with bounds, volume, mesh checks and file hashes. Existing output directories are preserved. CAD success does not define a material, boundary condition, motion law or physical body: attach the verified geometry through an explicit native configuration edit.

For long CAD work, geometry recipe.json --detach --root /workspace --json returns a job reference immediately. The MCP geometry operation also defaults to detached; set detach: false and an explicit workspace-relative output for synchronous generation. Both paths use the same CAD implementation and validation.

docs.title: Persistent execution
docs.text:
sphinxsim project project/config.json --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim preview project/config.json --with-particles --detach --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim run project/config.json --detach --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim job status reference.json --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim job continue reference.json --root /workspace --json
sphinxsim job results reference.json --root /workspace --json

--json/--detach select headless job publication for run/preview. For the original interactive or off-screen screenshot workflow, keep using native preview without those options; incompatible GUI/job option combinations are rejected rather than silently ignored.

Save the returned data.reference object as reference.json:

{"job_id": "<UUID>", "request_sha256": "<SHA-256 of the frozen request>"}

Every later job command requires that complete reference. Results, status, logs, continue and cancel do not infer a current or latest job. MCP submission requires the reviewed inventory from project_inspect; changed inputs are rejected before execution. Use a stable submission_id (CLI: --submission-id UUID) to retry the same frozen submission; reusing it with different inputs or policy is rejected.

Particle preview retains one native instance until its explicit lease expires. job continue continues that instance once; retries do not start another solver. An expired lease requires an explicitly requested new execution of frozen inputs. Disconnection and stopping agent operations do not cancel calculations. Explicit job cancel requests cancellation from the live supervisor, never a stored PID. Interrupted supervisors are reported; inputs are not automatically replayed.

An external scheduler can execute an already-frozen request without creating a second local queue:

sphinxsim run --request request.json --output /execution --json
sphinxsim preview --request particle-request.json --output /execution --json

The work directory must contain project/ matching the JSON inventory. run accepts kind run; preview accepts geometry or particles. The request schema is execution in contracts-v1.json. The caller owns resource isolation, supervision and a fresh execution directory. Retained particles accept the explicit control.json command bound to their attempt; the work directory and request identify all inputs. Reusing an existing solver output is rejected. No arbitrary executable is accepted.

A trusted Python host can call sphinxsim.cli.main(argv, publish_json=callback) for frozen --request execution. The callback receives (path, document) before manifest/status JSON becomes visible and must publish atomically or raise. The default is the native atomic JSON writer. This permits an external host to translate its wire envelope without a second output tree or a race after publication. There is no CLI/MCP argument that loads executable callbacks; only trusted embedding code can supply one. Resource hashing, numerical buffers and native configuration admission remain the native implementation's responsibility.

docs.title: Native desktop
docs.text:
sphinxsim desktop serve project/config.json --root /workspace \
  --reference-file /workspace/.native-desktop.json --locale en --theme dark

This opens the native Qt editor and simulation actions. Preview and particle generation are explicit actions; opening a window does not submit a computation. The new reference file is owner-readable only and contains a short-lived authenticated loopback connection. Treat it as a credential. The server binds an ephemeral loopback port, not a public listener. Closing the window releases the listener and leaves independent jobs running.

CLI desktop status request.json --desktop-reference ... --json reads current state; {} is sufficient for status. Mutating commands name the observed instance_id, version and an automation_id. Applying or saving uses the raw expected_hash; preview/particles also require a stable submission_id UUID. apply accepts a complete reviewed native configuration. CAD generation only produces a candidate: applying it is a separate explicit configuration operation.

Human edits invalidate old versions. Unsaved edits are preserved on conflicts. desktop stop fences the named automation scope, without canceling jobs or blocking human editing. A fresh turn observes again and uses a fresh scope. Continue/cancel/result require an explicit job reference. Historical result views show the frozen configuration and latest verified output; edit explicitly returns to the source configuration. Refresh failures retain the previous scene. Screenshots capture the native window as PNG on a supported display.

Remote mouse/keyboard, focus observation, resolution changes, video streaming, browser embedding and provider-specific recovery belong to external integrations. They are not simulated by the native application commands.

docs.title: Results and limits
docs.text:
Published manifests, buffers and original VTP files are verified before exposure. Only complete VTP snapshots are decoded; unfinished files are retried. Results can remain available after a failed execution and are marked partial when incomplete. Bodies can be fluids or continua; counts may vary per frame and fields are taken from actual output. results_inspect returns bounded summaries and verified resource references, not every frame in the model context.

Quality reports inspect saved outputs: finite data, output time coverage, particle counts, supported domain checks and penetration into supported static solid geometry. They state tolerances and not_evaluated checks. Open boundaries, native scaling, missing surfaces and insufficient data restrict interpretation. Source routing evidence, schema admission, successful execution and physical accuracy are different claims. No report certifies convergence or all coupled physics combinations; global extrema do not locate a pressure hotspot.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use the existing project build, install and test entry points:

python -m pip install -e '.[dev,cad,mcp,results,visualization]'
pytest tests/ -v
ctest --test-dir build-integrated --output-on-failure -L simulation_class

The native Linux CI installs the extras and runs real OCCT, stdio MCP, native particle/continue/lease and J2 material-builder tests. It also runs an opt-in real Qt/VTK window and PNG test under Xvfb with a CPU renderer. Without bindings, local native tests skip explicitly; SPHINXSIM_REQUIRE_NATIVE_TESTS=1 turns that absence into failure. SPHINXSIM_DESKTOP_TESTS=1 enables the real-window test when a display and bindings are available. Qt editor tests alone do not establish GPU or remote-desktop end-to-end behavior.

docs.title: CLI Usage Guide
docs.text:
SPHinXsim provides a command-line interface for building, validating, updating, and running SPH simulations. This guide covers all available commands and workflows.

Structured JSON, CadQuery modeling, persistent execution and MCP use the same CLI. See Native CLI and external agents.

docs.title: AI-assisted workflows
docs.text:
Use the interactive shell's generate, update, and explore commands for prompt-assisted configuration authoring. Provider selection is shared through SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER; see LLM testing for setup examples.

For a graphical workflow with an embedded Chat panel, reviewed configuration proposals, and Preview, start the Workbench:

python -m sphinxsim workbench

For durable AgentCAE calibration, start with python -m sphinxsim agent --help. The default workflow requires explicit approval before it runs a solver. The agent stores its state in a workspace so you can inspect, approve, resume, or report a workflow in a later process. See AgentCAE calibration for a complete example and the supported workflow scope.

docs.title: Shell auto-completion
docs.text:
Generate completion scripts directly from the CLI:

sphinxsim --generate-completion bash
sphinxsim --generate-completion zsh
sphinxsim --generate-completion fish

You can evaluate the script for the current shell session:

# bash
eval "$(sphinxsim --generate-completion bash)"

# zsh
eval "$(sphinxsim --generate-completion zsh)"

# fish
sphinxsim --generate-completion fish | source

For persistent completion, add the command to your shell startup file (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or ~/.config/fish/config.fish).

Troubleshooting: - If completion is not active in the current terminal, reload your shell config:

# bash
source ~/.bashrc

# zsh
source ~/.zshrc

# fish
source ~/.config/fish/config.fish
  • For zsh, ensure completion is initialized before evaluating the script:
autoload -Uz compinit
compinit
eval "$(sphinxsim --generate-completion zsh)"
  • To verify script output quickly:
sphinxsim --generate-completion bash | head

docs.title: Interactive shell mode (recommended)
docs.text:
The easiest way to get started is the interactive shell:

sphinxsim shell

This opens an interactive prompt where you can enter commands sequentially:

> generate "water dam break simulation" config.json
✓ Config generated and written to .../.build-temp/config.json
✓ Schema validation passed

> validate
Configuration: WaterBody (fluid) + WallBoundary (solid)
  Domain: [0, 0] to [5.37, 5.37]
  Resolution: 0.025 m
  End time: 0.5 s
  Gravity: [0, -1] m/s²

> update "simulate for 2 s"
✓ Updated config written to .../.build-temp/config.json
✓ Schema validation passed

> explore what bodies and materials does this simulation support?
SPHinXsim supports fluid, continuum, and solid body definitions, with schema-validated material types.

> validate
Configuration: WaterBody (fluid) + WallBoundary (solid)
  Domain: [0, 0] to [5.37, 5.37]
  Resolution: 0.025 m
  End time: 2.0 s
  Gravity: [0, -1] m/s²

> run
✅ Simulation configuration loaded
✅ Simulation initialized
🚀 Running simulation...

> update "water flow with 5 mm resolution"
> update "water flow with 5 mm resolution"
✓ Updated config written to .../.build-temp/config.json
✓ Schema validation passed

> exit
Goodbye!

On interactive terminals, press Tab to complete shell commands and file arguments (such as load and generate paths). Use the Up and Down arrow keys to navigate commands entered during the current shell session.

In shell mode you can also use slash-prefixed commands without quotes around the description, for example:

sphinxsim> /generate water dam break simulation config.json
sphinxsim> /update simulate for 2 s

docs.title: Shell commands
docs.text:
Inside the shell, you can use the following commands:

Command Description load FILE Load and validate an existing config file generate "description" FILE Generate a new config and write it to FILE update "instruction" Modify the loaded config with an instruction (e.g., "change end time to 5 s") update --patch-mode "instruction" Apply operation-based patch updates update --patch-mode --dry-run "instruction" Preview patch update without writing update --patch-mode --strict false "instruction" Use non-strict patch apply behavior explore "question" Ask the configured LLM questions about the simulator schema and capabilities validate Reload the loaded file from disk and validate it preview Render an interactive geometry/BC preview of the loaded config preview --with-particles Also run particle generation and overlay the latest generated particles per body preview --screenshot FILE Save a screenshot to FILE instead of opening an interactive window continue-to-run [--refresh-interval SECONDS] Build, initialize, and run the simulation retained by the most recent particle preview; collect snapshots every 10 seconds by default and play each batch at up to 25 FPS run Build and execute the loaded config run --with-animation Preview generated particles, continue that same simulation, and animate its snapshots replay Replay particle snapshots from the latest successful animated run at up to 25 FPS help Show available commands exit Quit the shell

Notes: - sphinxsim shell starts with no file loaded. - Relative file paths inside the shell resolve from the current directory first, then fall back to .build-temp/. - In shell mode, slash-prefixed commands are also accepted, e.g. /generate water dam break simulation config.json or /update simulate for 2 s. - validate always reloads from disk, so external edits are picked up immediately. - In shell mode, preview keeps a persistent window and returns control to the prompt. Running preview again updates the same window. - preview --with-particles retains its generated-particle simulation for one immediate continue-to-run command. Any other command discards that retained simulation. - run without options is unchanged. run --with-animation performs the equivalent of preview --with-particles followed by continue-to-run. - continue-to-run --refresh-interval SECONDS sets the delay between checks for new body-state VTP files; the default is 10 seconds. At each check, all available snapshots are played in sequence at up to 25 FPS, then the preview waits for the next interval before collecting another batch. When the simulation finishes, the preview promptly checks and plays any remaining snapshots. Live refresh requires the Qt-backed persistent preview (pyvistaqt with PySide6 or PyQt5); the simulation still runs when that preview is unavailable, but its particles are not updated live. - After a successful run --with-animation or continue-to-run, use replay to play the recorded particle snapshots again. Replay opens a Qt-backed window if needed, keeps the current camera view fixed while particles animate, and is capped at 25 FPS. - For responsive persistent preview, install pyvistaqt and a Qt backend (PySide6 or PyQt5). - In the Qt-backed preview, edit settings in the searchable property tree on the right and press Ctrl+S; only then are changes validated, saved, and rendered. Click the Setting ▾ column header for Expand, Collapse, Revert, and Reload. To modify list entries, right-click the list row or entry and choose an available action from its context menu. If preview would reset unapplied edits, it asks for confirmation first. - To switch configurations while the Preview window remains open, run load OTHER.json followed by preview; the property editor is rebound to the newly loaded file. - If the persistent Preview window is closed, run preview again to create a new window.

docs.title: Geometry update workflow
docs.text:
Shell workflows do not keep a persistent geometry lock state.

  • Geometry changes can be applied with update whenever needed.
  • After changing geometry, rerun validate, preview, or run to rebuild from the updated JSON config.
  • run always rebuilds the simulation from the current config before executing it.

In non-interactive direct commands (sphinxsim update ...), the same config-first behavior applies: the updated JSON is the source of truth for the next preview or run.

docs.title: Direct commands (non-interactive)
docs.text: You can also run individual commands directly:

docs.title: Generate
docs.text:
Create a new simulation config from a natural language description:

sphinxsim generate "2D water dam break with 0.5 m/s initial velocity" --output config.json

This: 1. Sends your description to the LLM provider (mock by default, or Ollama if configured) 2. Receives a JSON config in response 3. Validates the config against strict schemas 4. Saves the result to config.json 5. Prints a summary

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
Check an existing config without modifying it:

sphinxsim validate config.json

This displays: - Simulation type (fluid_dynamics, continuum_dynamics, or coupled) - List of bodies and their material types - Domain bounds and resolution - Solver parameters (end time, output interval, etc.) - Any validation errors

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
Modify an existing config with natural language instructions:

sphinxsim update config.json "increase end time to 10 s" --output config_updated.json

This: 1. Loads the existing config 2. Sends it to the LLM provider along with your instruction 3. Receives a modified JSON config 4. Validates the updated config 5. Saves the result to config_updated.json

docs.title: Explore
docs.text:
Ask the configured LLM questions about the simulator schema, supported bodies, materials, and workflow behavior:

sphinxsim explore "What body types are valid in SimulationConfig?"

This: 1. Sends your question and schema context to the selected LLM provider 2. Returns a plain-text explanation of the simulator schema and capabilities 3. Uses the same provider selection as generate and update

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Execute a validated simulation:

sphinxsim run config.json

This: 1. Validates the config 2. Builds SPHinXsys simulation components in C++ 3. Runs the simulation 4. Saves output to build-integrated/output

docs.title: Preview
docs.text:
Render an interactive 3-D geometry/BC preview before running the solver:

sphinxsim preview config.json

This: 1. Validates the config 2. Attempts to invoke buildGeometries() from the C++ extension to produce accurate VTP meshes 3. Opens an interactive PyVista window with colour-coded bodies, oriented boxes, and annotations

Options:

Flag Description --with-particles Also run particle generation and overlay the latest generated particles per body. Hides regular shapes; keeps oriented boxes and annotations. --off-screen Render off-screen (no window) — useful for automated testing --screenshot FILE / -s FILE Save a screenshot to FILE instead of opening a window. Implies --off-screen.

Requires the optional [visualization] extra:

pip install sphinxsim[visualization]

For responsive persistent shell preview:

pip install pyvistaqt PySide6
# or: pip install pyvistaqt PyQt5

See Visualization for full details.

docs.title: Example 1: Quick iteration with the shell
docs.text:
sphinxsim shell
> generate "2D water dam break, domain 5m x 5m, resolution 2.5cm" config.json
> validate
> run
> exit

docs.title: Example 2: Compare two configurations
docs.text:
sphinxsim generate "water dam break" --output config_v1.json
sphinxsim validate config_v1.json

sphinxsim generate "water dam break with faster gravity" --output config_v2.json
sphinxsim validate config_v2.json

# Then run the version you prefer:
sphinxsim run config_v1.json

docs.title: Example 3: External editing loop in shell
docs.text:
sphinxsim shell
> load config.json
> validate
# edit config.json in your editor while shell remains open
> validate
> update "change particle spacing to 1 cm"
> explore what materials can I use for solid bodies?
> validate
> run

docs.title: Example 4: Batch process with direct commands
docs.text:
for desc in "water dam break" "sloshing tank" "wave propagation"; do
  sphinxsim generate "$desc" --output "config_$desc.json"
  sphinxsim validate "config_$desc.json"
done

docs.title: Example 5: Preview before running
docs.text:
sphinxsim shell
> generate "2D heat transfer in a channel" config.json
> validate
> preview                   # inspect geometry and BCs interactively
> preview --with-particles  # overlay generated particles (hides shapes)
> preview --screenshot preview.png   # save a screenshot for a report
> run
> exit

docs.title: Example 6: Geometry edit loop in shell
docs.text:
sphinxsim shell
> load config.json
> run
> update "water flow with 5 mm resolution"
> validate
> preview
> run

docs.title: Example 7: Soil column-collapse workflow (continuum dynamics)
docs.text:
# Validate and run the soil benchmark config
sphinxsim validate tests/test_simulation/test_2d_simulation/data/column_collapse.json
sphinxsim run tests/test_simulation/test_2d_simulation/data/column_collapse.json

# Optional: iterate in shell
sphinxsim shell
> load tests/test_simulation/test_2d_simulation/data/column_collapse.json
> explore what material fields are required for plastic_continuum?
> validate
> run

This case uses continuum dynamics with a plastic_continuum material model for granular/soil behavior.

docs.title: LLM provider selection
docs.text: By default, sphinxsim uses a local mock LLM that works offline. To use a different provider:

docs.title: Use Ollama (local LLM inference)
docs.text:
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_MODEL=qwen2.5:3b
sphinxsim generate "water dam break"

First, ensure Ollama is running:

ollama serve
# In another terminal:
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b

docs.title: Use OpenAI
docs.text:
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=openai
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_API_KEY=sk-...
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_MODEL=gpt-4
sphinxsim generate "water dam break"

docs.title: Use NVIDIA NIM (OpenAI-compatible API)
docs.text:
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=nvidia_nim
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_API_KEY=nvapi-...
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_MODEL=meta/muse-glimmer-30b
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_BASE_URL=https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1
sphinxsim generate "water dam break"

docs.title: Use mock (default)
docs.text:
export SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=mock
sphinxsim generate "water dam break"

docs.title: Output locations
docs.text:
• Generated configs: Printed to stdout unless --output is provided
  • Generated configs with --output: Written to the exact path you provide (relative to your current directory)
  • Shell-generated configs: Saved to the FILE argument used by generate "..." FILE (resolved from current directory first, then .build-temp/)
  • Explore answers: Printed to stdout; no files are written
  • Simulation output: Saved under .build-temp/test_simulation/ (runtime output root)
  • Temporary files: Stored in .build-temp/

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
If config generation or validation fails:

  1. Generation fails: The LLM response did not match the expected JSON schema. Check the error message for details, or try rephrasing your description.
  2. Validation fails: The config violates a schema constraint (e.g., body type mismatch). Use sphinxsim validate to see which field is invalid.
  3. Explore fails: The LLM could not answer using the schema context. Rephrase the question to focus on supported bodies, materials, solver settings, or CLI workflow.
  4. Execution fails: The config is valid but the simulation failed. Check simulation output in .build-temp/test_simulation/.

cd SPHinXsim

docs.title: Install vcpkg
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg.git ../vcpkg
../vcpkg/bootstrap-vcpkg.sh

docs.title: Install C/C++ Dependencies
docs.text:
../vcpkg/vcpkg install --clean-after-build openblas[dynamic-arch] --allow-unsupported
../vcpkg/vcpkg install --clean-after-build \
  eigen3 \
  tbb \
  boost-program-options \
  boost-geometry \
  simbody \
  spdlog \
  gtest \
  pybind11 \
  nlohmann-json

docs.title: Configure and Build
docs.text:
For a pip-first workflow, install directly from source (this builds C++ extensions via CMake):

CMAKE_ARGS="-D CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$(pwd)/../vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake" \
python3 -m pip install -v -e ".[dev,visualization]"

Optional manual CMake workflow:

cmake --preset integrated-build-release \
  -D CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$(pwd)/../vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake" \
  -D Python3_EXECUTABLE="$(which python3)"
cmake --build --preset integrated-build-release --parallel "$(nproc)"

To avoid issue of insufficient memory, you need to pick the number of "$(nproc)" based on your RAM. Rough rule: ~1.5–2 GB RAM per job for C++ projects. For example you can build with

cmake --build --preset integrated-build-release --parallel 4

Install compiled C++ extension modules into the active Python environment:

cmake --install build-integrated --prefix "$(python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.prefix)')"

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

Run Python tests:

python -m pytest tests/ examples/ -v

Run C++ simulation tests:

ctest --test-dir build-integrated --output-on-failure -R "test_(2d|3d)_simulation$"

docs.title: LLM Testing
docs.text: This project uses two distinct LLM test paths so local development can exercise both a mock backend and a live Ollama backend, while CI stays fully deterministic.

docs.title: Test matrix
docs.text: Test area Local CI tests/test_ollama_llm.py Mocked only Mocked only tests/test_ollama_llm_integration.py Live Ollama when available, otherwise skipped Skipped examples/test_nlp_to_simulation.py Mocked case plus live Ollama case when available Mocked case only, live Ollama skipped

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Local development typically uses setup-local-env.sh to set:

  • SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
  • OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
  • OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:3b

CI sets SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=mock so the workflow never depends on an external API or a running Ollama server.

docs.title: How to run locally
docs.text:
To exercise the mock and Ollama paths locally:

# Test with mock LLM (no Ollama needed)
pytest tests/test_ollama_llm.py -v

# Test with live Ollama (requires Ollama running locally)
pytest tests/test_ollama_llm_integration.py -v

# Run end-to-end example with both mock and Ollama
pytest examples/test_nlp_to_simulation.py -v

# Or use the interactive shell with Ollama
source setup-local-env.sh
sphinxsim shell
# Then issue commands like: generate ..., update ..., explore ..., validate, run

docs.title: How CI behaves
docs.text: CI runs the mocked tests everywhere and skips the live Ollama cases automatically. This keeps the pipeline stable while still validating the example workflow and the Ollama adapter logic that does not require a live server.

docs.title: Interactive shell with Ollama
docs.text:
For interactive development, use the shell mode with Ollama:

source setup-local-env.sh  # Sets SPHINXSIM_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama and other vars
sphinxsim shell

Inside the shell, you can generate and update configs using the live Ollama backend:

> generate "2D water dam break simulation" config.json
